title: iTaskSense: Task-Oriented Object Detection in Resource-Constrained Environments
problem: Efficient task-oriented object detection on edge/resource-constrained devices; conventional models require extensive datasets and struggle with generalization to diverse real-world scenarios.
motivation: Autonomous systems (drones, vehicles, healthcare, industrial) need efficient intelligent sensing; vision-language models have high computational cost; edge devices require low-latency, efficient task-specific detection.
method: iTask framework leverages LLMs to generalize from limited samples via abstract knowledge graph encoding task attributes. Two configuration models: (1) distilled task-specific vision transformer for defined tasks (15% higher accuracy); (2) quantized model for multi-task robustness. Custom hardware acceleration circuit supports real-time edge processing.
key_novelty: LLM-based knowledge graph generation for few-shot task-oriented object detection, combined with dual-configuration vision transformers (distilled task-specific and quantized multi-task) and hardware acceleration.
contributions: iTask framework leveraging LLMs to generate abstract knowledge graphs for task-specific detection
Dual-configuration approach: task-specific distilled ViT and quantized multi-task ViT
Custom hardware accelerator for edge real-time processing
3.5x speedup and 40% energy reduction vs. GPU-based implementations

metrics.accuracy: 15% higher accuracy in task-specific configuration over quantized baseline

primary_theme: Task-oriented object detection on edge devices via LLM knowledge graphs and hardware acceleration
